state_tracker.name: City of Yes for Housing Opportunity
state_tracker.what: Universal Affordability Preference: ~20% more floor area in R6-R10 when the extra space is permanently affordable at a 60% AMI average; parking minimums removed or reduced by zone; ADUs and small-lot infill; town-center zoning (housing above stores) in low-density districts; office-to-residential conversions citywide for buildings built before 1991.
state_tracker.play: Every R6-R10 lot on the deal board already carries the UAP path. Low-density districts (R1-R5) now allow ADUs and 3-5 story 'town center' buildings on commercial streets: a separate screen worth adding.

state_tracker.name: 485-x (Affordable Neighborhoods for New Yorkers)
state_tracker.what: Replaces 421-a. Option B (6-99 units): 20% affordable at 80% AMI avg, 35-year exemption, no construction wage rule. Option C (6-10 units): 10-year exemption, half stabilized. Start construction by June 15, 2034.
state_tracker.play: Underwritten on every NYC deal. The 6-10 unit Option C is the solo-builder path.

state_tracker.name: Faith-Based Affordable Housing Act (S3397B / A3647B)
state_tracker.what: Would let religious corporations build apartments as of right on their land: outside NYC up to 30 units/acre (50 if subsidized) and +20 ft height, with 20% at 80% AMI; in NYC, height and coverage of nearby taller districts with 25% at 60% AMI. 60-day local approval, no parking minimums, SEQRA EIS exemption with a Phase I.
state_tracker.play: If it passes, every faith-owned lot on the board (NYC filter: Faith-owned) and every church parcel in Westchester becomes a by-right site. Watch the bill; line up congregations now.

state_tracker.name: Pro-Housing Communities certification
state_tracker.what: Municipalities that certify (and commit to growing housing stock or adopting pro-housing zoning) get priority for state discretionary funds. Certified towns are the ones adopting ADU, mixed-use and TOD changes.
state_tracker.play: Cross-check any suburban deal's town against the certified list; a certified town is likelier to approve density and to have a zoning change in process.

state_tracker.name: HB 8002 Housing Growth Act
state_tracker.what: As-of-right middle and multifamily housing in qualifying transit-oriented districts; municipalities encouraged to adopt Priority Housing Development Zones (as-of-right multifamily); parking requirements cut for projects of 16 or fewer units and capped above that; harder to petition against zoning amendments; mandatory municipal or regional Housing Growth Plans (Fairfield County towns by June 2029).
state_tracker.play: Stamford, Norwalk, Darien, Westport and Greenwich station areas are the first places to look for TOD-district sites. Track each town's Housing Growth Plan and PHDZ adoption on the news radar.

state_tracker.name: CGS 8-30g Affordable Housing Appeals
state_tracker.what: In towns under 10% affordable stock, a project with 30% deed-restricted units can appeal a zoning denial and the town must prove a public-health or safety reason to deny. Greenwich, Darien, New Canaan, Westport, Ridgefield are under 10%; Stamford and New Haven are exempt.
state_tracker.play: The CT board's lever. Sewer availability decides density far more than the statute.

state_tracker.name: Fourth Round affordable housing obligations (2025-2035)
state_tracker.what: Every municipality had to adopt a Housing Element and Fair Share Plan by June 30, 2025 and the implementing zoning (inclusionary and overlay zones, redevelopment plans) by March 15, 2026. Towns that miss lose immunity from exclusionary-zoning (builder's remedy) litigation.
state_tracker.play: The adopted ordinances are new overlay zones with real density, often on commercial corridors. Pull each Bergen/Hudson town's HEFSP for the site list; towns out of compliance are builder's-remedy targets.

state_tracker.name: Local Redevelopment and Housing Law (40A:12A) + Long Term Tax Exemption (40A:20)
state_tracker.what: A municipality can designate an Area in Need of Redevelopment, adopt a redevelopment plan with its own density, and convey sites directly to a designated redeveloper with a ~30-year PILOT.
state_tracker.play: The NJ board's lever. New redevelopment-plan adoptions show up on the news radar first.
